title: Molecular diversity of visual pigments in the butterfly Papilio glaucus
why: Would give the Eastern Tiger Swallowtail's own opsin set and so how many colour classes it can have, which the swallowtail rows now borrow from Papilio xuthus.

title: Six opsins from the butterfly Papilio glaucus: molecular phylogenetic evidence for paralogous origin of red-sensitive visual pigments in insects
why: Gives the sequence evidence for the red-sensitive opsin in the species Florida people photograph most among swallowtails.

title: Eye morphology and visual acuity in the pipevine swallowtail (Battus philenor) studied with a new method of ommatidial mapping
journal: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society
why: Would give a measured acuity and ommatidial map for a swallowtail met in Florida; the abstract alone gives no figures.

title: Allometry and resolution of bee eyes (Apoidea)
why: Tabulates eye parameters across many bee species, so it could replace the honeybee's figures with values for bumblebees, carpenter bees and sweat bees.

authors: Macuda T, Gegear RJ, Laverty TM, Timney B
title: Behavioural assessment of visual acuity in bumblebees (Bombus impatiens)
why: The Common Eastern Bumble Bee's behavioural acuity; would give the bumblebee a measured figure of its own.

authors: Peitsch D, Fietz A, Hertel H, de Souza J, Ventura DF, Menzel R
title: The spectral input systems of hymenopteran insects and their receptor-based colour vision
why: Receptor peaks for 43 hymenopteran species; would settle which bees and wasps share the honeybee's three classes under carry rule 2.

authors: Chatterjee P, Mohan U, Krishna S
title: Evolutionary constraints on flicker fusion frequency in Lepidoptera
why: Flicker fusion values for many butterflies and moths; would replace one swallowtail's 107 Hz with figures for the Monarch, Gulf Fritillary and Cabbage White.

title: Animal Eyes, 2nd edition, chapters 7 and 8 (apposition and superposition compound eyes)
why: Textbook values for acuity and sensitivity of butterfly, moth, fly and dragonfly eyes, to fill rows no paper in the collection reaches.

authors: Guignard Q, Goodwin JTL, Kimoto T, et al.
title: Characterising spectral sensitivity and the role of sunlight intensity in Japanese beetle (Popillia japonica) behaviour
why: Spectral sensitivity of a scarab met in Florida gardens; the licence says open access, so try the publisher page first.

authors: Qiu K-R, Wang K, Dai Y-F, et al.
title: UV2 and LW opsin genes mediate phototactic responses in the Asian lady beetle, Harmonia axyridis
why: Names the opsin classes of the Asian Lady Beetle, the third most recorded species in the world list.

title: Proximate constraints on intruder detection in the dragonfly Perithemis tenera
journal: Annals of the Entomological Society of America
why: How far an Eastern Amberwing detects an intruder; would give a skimmer its own detection distance.

authors: Zaccardi G, Kelber A, Sison-Mangus MP, Briscoe AD
title: Color discrimination in the red range with only one long-wavelength sensitive opsin
why: Behavioural red discrimination in a nymphalid with one long-wavelength opsin; settles whether red vision needs more than one.

authors: Menzel R, Steinmann E, de Souza J, Backhaus W
title: Spectral sensitivity of photoreceptors and colour vision in the solitary bee, Osmia rufa
why: A solitary bee's receptor peaks; gives a second bee family beside the honeybee for the sweat and leafcutter bees.

title: Rapid spatial learning in a velvet ant (Dasymutilla coccineohirta)
why: Velvet ants are common in Florida and are lent the bee view; this is one of few papers on their vision-guided behaviour.

authors: Maredia KM, Gage SH, Landis DA, Wirth TM
title: Visual response of Coccinella septempunctata, Hippodamia parenthesis (Coleoptera: Coccinellidae) to colors
why: Colour choice in two ladybird species; would test the seven-spot ladybird's carry to the Asian Lady Beetle.

authors: Windsor SP, Bomphrey RJ, Taylor GK
title: Vision-based flight control in the hawkmoth Hyles lineata
journal: Journal of the Royal Society Interface
why: Open licence; hawkmoth flight control gives the White-lined Sphinx's own visual-motor figures.

authors: Somanathan H, Warrant EJ, Borges RM, Wallen R, Kelber A
title: Resolution and sensitivity of the eyes of the Asian honeybees Apis florea, Apis cerana and Apis dorsata
why: Eye resolution for three further honeybee species; shows how much one bee species' figures vary within the genus.

title: Complex social behaviour can select for variability in visual features: a case study in Polistes wasps
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
why: Face recognition in Polistes; relevant to the paper wasp rows of the bee view.
